briefing.headline: The three-day mandate is predicted to nearly double departures over the next 12 months, from about 538 to 989 of 5,000 employees (about 450 more people, +91%).
briefing.most_at_risk: Caregivers (+126%), long commuters (+122%), and managers and mid-level staff (+114% and +111%) react worst because the mandate costs them the most hours and family logistics, while juniors (+69%) and short commuters (+63%) react mildest and partly see value in office time.
risks: The exits will be slow, not sudden: nearly every voice says 'comply and quietly look,' so departures will land over months whenever a flexible competitor makes an offer, and early compliance numbers will understate the damage.

The losses fall heaviest on managers and mid-level staff, the people who hold team knowledge and who would also have to enforce the badge reviews, which weakens leadership exactly when the change needs managing.

Badge tracking reads as distrust even to employees who are fine with three days, so it lowers goodwill among the people who stay. VP-only exceptions will likely create a backlog and uneven decisions, since several at-risk employees say they will ask for one first.
design_changes: Drop individual badge reviews with managers, or limit them to team-level attendance, so the policy is about collaboration, not surveillance.
Let each team pick its own anchor days, and set clear published exception criteria (for example, long commutes or caregiving) that line managers can approve, with VP review only for edge cases.
Lengthen the 90-day runway or phase the policy in for long-commute and caregiving employees, and pilot it with a few teams before applying it company-wide.
briefing.confidence: low, because every modelled voice points the same way (more job-hunting, mainly among caregivers and long commuters), but the figures rest on about two simulated voices per group, so treat the +91% as a sign of serious risk rather than a number to plan headcount against.

subgroup_checks.claim: Bigger rise for mid and senior managers
